audit_findings.title: Acquisition-led growth may be treated as free
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,372.5m net acquisition cash outlays in 2023-2025; 2025 sales growth included 4 percentage points from acquisitions/divestitures; base and bull operating PV exceed bear by $1,347m and $2,926m, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings increase historical OE and may support projected growth, while acquisition payments are excluded from OE and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s historical growth has included, and the Company’s future growth is likely to continue to include, acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that acquisitions have contributed materially to growth and required cash outlays comparable to the scenario growth premiums. They do not demonstrate that the projected 3% or 6% growth requires acquisitions, but if either forecast embeds continued acquired growth without its funding cost, the valuation overstates distributable owner earnings by a material amount.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic from acquired OE for each historical year; identify the organic growth rate supporting each scenario; rerun any acquisition-dependent scenario with forecast acquisition payments, share issuance, incremental debt interest, or an equivalent reinvestment charge.

audit_findings.title: Growth may omit working-capital reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $58.4m organic operating-working-capital increase in 2025 and $65.5m in the first six months of 2026; respectively 9.3% and 10.5% of $625.1m anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Required increases in receivables and inventory reduce OE available for distribution as sales grow.
audit_findings.evidence: Apart from these items, the primary drivers of the change in Operating working capital were higher receivables, driven by price and the timing of shipments, and higher inventories, which increased early in the year to support planned production.
audit_findings.explanation: The stated valuation method identifies a capital-expenditure deduction but no incremental working-capital deduction. Filed organic working-capital increases are large relative to anchor OE, and the June 2026 filing attributes the increase partly to higher volumes, price, and planned production. Some amount may be timing-related, but omitting a recurring requirement is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Build a normalized incremental operating-working-capital requirement from multi-year organic changes relative to organic sales growth, exclude documented timing items, and rerun the growth scenarios with that annual reinvestment deduction.

audit_findings.title: Cash interest may be double counted
audit_findings.mechanism: Investment income left in equity-level OE would be capitalized in operating PV while the related $621.3m of cash is also added through the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense - net increased primarily due to the impact of higher debt outstanding in connection with financing the acquisition of Mott.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation says portfolio interest income was purged, so double counting is not demonstrated. The filings report net interest expense rather than a complete gross-interest reconciliation: 2025 net interest expense was $64.4m, cash interest paid was $72.2m, and first-half 2026 net interest expense included $0.6m of tariff-refund interest. These figures do not establish how much recurring cash or investment income remained in OE, so materiality cannot be determined.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile gross interest expense, recurring cash and investment income, tax effects, and OE adjustments for every historical year, especially 2025; rerun the valuation for any after-tax investment income not removed.

audit_findings.title: Retirement deficits may remain ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $60.1m funded deficit at December 31, 2025 and $5.6m expected 2026 defined-benefit and postretirement contributions; $60.1m equals about $0.80 per diluted share and 0.64% of $9,404m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unfunded retirement obligation not represented by normalized OE is a senior claim requiring a bridge deduction or future OE funding.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to contribute approximately $ 4.6 million to its defined benefit plans and $ 1.0 million to its other postretirement benefit plans in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed funded-status measurement totals $60.1m: $4.5m for U.S. pensions, $38.0m for non-U.S. pensions, and $17.6m for other benefits. Even deducting the entire amount would reduce base value by only about $0.80 per share, versus base value of $125.58 per share and market price of $223.74. The June 2026 filing does not provide an updated funded status, but the disclosed scale is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the next updated funded status and whether contributions exceeding pension expense are already represented in OE; deduct only an uncovered deficit if it grows materially beyond the filed $60.1m.

audit_findings.title: Micro-LAM earnout is omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.2m June 30, 2026 fair-value liability, with a $12.0m contractual maximum; approximately $0.02 per share at fair value or $0.16 per share at the maximum
audit_findings.mechanism: Contingent acquisition consideration is a cash claim ahead of common equity and belongs in the equity bridge unless already charged to forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the acquisition of Micro-LAM, the Company entered into an earnout agreement that may require it to make future cash consideration payments of up to $ 12.0 million based upon the achievement of certain financial performance targets from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated because the latest filing carries a $1.2m contingent-consideration liability while the bridge contains no deduction. Its fair value is about 0.013% of $9,404m base equity value; even the $12.0m maximum is only about 0.13%. Neither amount could materially change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Add the latest $1.2m fair-value liability to the bridge reconciliation and continue monitoring remeasurement; rerun only if the probability-weighted liability rises materially toward or beyond the $12.0m maximum.

audit_findings.title: Foreign-cash tax friction may be ignored
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.5m estimated unrecognized deferred tax liability on $90.2m of permanently reinvested earnings; about $0.18 per share, 2.2% of the $621.3m cash bridge, and 0.14% of $9,404m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Taxes or withholding required to make foreign cash available would reduce the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount of unrecognized deferred income tax liabilities on currently permanently reinvested earnings is estimated to be $ 13.5 million and $ 11.0 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Face-value treatment could overstate accessible cash, but the filed estimate associated with permanently reinvested earnings is only $13.5m. Deducting that full amount would reduce base value by approximately $0.18 per share. The company also reported substantial 2023-2025 repatriations without incremental income-tax expense other than foreign-exchange effects, further limiting evidence of a material present haircut.
audit_findings.action: Map the $514.0m of June 2026 cash held outside the United States by jurisdiction and tax basis, then deduct only documented withholding, foreign-income-tax, or distribution costs exceeding amounts already recognized.
